candidate.title: HiTS-FLIP
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina schematic of High-Throughput Sequencing–Fluorescent Ligand Interaction Profiling (HiTS-FLIP): preparation and sequencing of flowcell DNA, primer-directed duplex rebuilding, fluorescent protein binding, depicted pre-scan handling, and flowcell fluorescence imaging. This is one workflow with no depicted alternative branches. The Nutiu et al. Gcn4p implementation resolves the pre-scan label; it does not add other assays or make its particular randomized library obligatory for every HiTS-FLIP experiment.

states.label: Target DNA sequences to be tested for protein binding
features: The left Protein binding site icon and pink Target sequence segment identify a DNA binding substrate; they are explanatory, not a separately transferred protein-DNA complex.

The library represents DNA sequence diversity for in vitro binding measurements. The paper describes genomic or random synthetic DNA and demonstrates randomized synthetic DNA; the diagram does not restrict the input origin.

Main text, HiTS-FLIP concept [b00007]
evidence.quote: 1) build and sequence ~100 million clusters of genomic or random synthetic DNA; 2) denature and wash away the second strand and rebuild double-stranded DNA; 3) introduce fluorescently-tagged protein to the flow cell; 4) after an optional two-minute wash step, quantify the binding to each cluster by visualizing fluorescence; and 5) map the bound clusters to corresponding sequences and analyze, yielding a comprehensive, quantitative landscape of binding specificity.

operations.label: Synthesize second strand with unmodified nucleotides
operations.description: Klenow extends the annealed primer to restore a double-stranded DNA binding substrate on the flowcell.
operations.mechanism: Primer-directed synthesis by Klenow using unmodified dNTPs. Klenow is a catalyst and the nucleotides supply the new strand, not additional independently processed biological targets.
operations.information_effect: Retains the known cluster sequence and position while restoring a duplex substrate for protein binding.

operations.label: Add fluorescently labeled ligand / Hybridize
operations.description: Fluorescent protein is introduced to the rebuilt duplex clusters and can bind DNA sites. The source term Hybridize here labels protein-DNA association, as clarified by the protein-binding paper; it does not denote another nucleic-acid strand synthesis.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, collection page heading and schematic caption all identify HiTS-FLIP. The full-text paper names this workflow and supports the sequenced-cluster/duplex-rebuilding/fluorescent-protein interface. All drawn operations belong to this one target, with the increasing-stringency label resolved explicitly at o_prescan. Klenow is a component and the associated kit name is not an alternative workflow.

corrections.diagram_observation: The source explicitly labels the panel after ligand binding Elute with increasing stringency, shows a white flow/elution symbol, retains the bound fluorescent protein on the flowcell duplex, and then points to Scan flowcell.
corrections.primary_statement: Nutiu et al. report adding fluorescent Gcn4p at several concentrations and imaging its binding to the same sequenced DNA clusters. They report a brief pre-imaging wash and similar results when it was omitted; Methods 5.10 repeats binding/imaging for increasing protein concentrations. This supports an optional wash before scanning, not an increasing-stringency elution series or collection and sequencing of an eluate. o_prescan and s_prescan use that primary-supported interpretation while preserving the drawn label and position.
